I am 37 years old, middle school educated, farming about 10 mu in Quzhou. My family depends on this land, and every yuan I spend on inputs has to come back with something extra. I don't have the money or the nerve to gamble on new ideas — I watch what works for my neighbors and mostly do the same.

It is early spring now. The wheat I planted last October is greening up, so my first job is to topdress it and get the irrigation going. I have 10 mu total. I will put 7 mu into the wheat-maize double crop — that is the safest system, everybody does it, and I know the sequence by heart. The other 3 mu I will plant cotton. Cotton is more work, especially the spraying, but the price has been decent and my wife and I can still handle the labor. We need the cash.

For the wheat, I bought improved seed from the seed station last autumn — the same variety my uncle uses. I already put down basal fertilizer before winter, and now at green-up I will topdress with urea. All together I figure about 12 kg of nitrogen per mu for the whole wheat season, plus a little compound fertilizer for P and K. I will irrigate four times: now at green-up, again at jointing, once at flowering, and one more at grain filling. The water costs money, but dry wheat is worthless. Three pesticide sprays should cover weeds and the main diseases. I rotary-tilled before planting last autumn, so nothing more needed now. If the weather holds, I expect about 500 kg per mu.

For the summer maize, I will plant hybrid seed right after the wheat comes off in early June — the window is only a few days, so no time for ploughing. No-tillage direct seeding is what everyone does now. I will apply less nitrogen than the extension pamphlet says, maybe 8 kg per mu, because the wheat already left something in the soil and fertilizer is expensive. A little P and K, three irrigations during summer, three pesticide rounds. I should get about 550 kg per mu if the rains don't fail.

The cotton goes on 3 mu. I will rotary-till and plant improved cotton seed in late April. Cotton needs more fertilizer than people think — I will put down about 10 kg nitrogen per mu, plus some phosphorus and potassium. The real headache is the spraying: bollworm, aphids, mites — I will need to spray about 12 times through the season. Two good irrigations at flowering and boll stage. Expected yield around 275 kg per mu of seed cotton. That is enough extra income to make it worth the trouble.

I thought about putting all 10 mu into wheat-maize to save labor, but 3 mu of cotton gives me a cash buffer if grain prices drop. I don't like debt, so I keep input costs tight, but I won't starve the crops either — a bad year hurts more than a good year helps.
